title: Access Control
text: Every entity Synapse benefactor - entity inherits permissions: Default Inheritance: New entities inherit permissions parent container Local ACLs: create custom sharing settings, entity becomes benefactor Permission Resolution: Synapse traverses hierarchy find benefactor ACL settings

title: Access Control
text: Synapse supports several permission types can combined: READ: View entity metadata basic information DOWNLOAD: Download files data (requires READ) UPDATE: Modify entity metadata upload new file versions CREATE: Create new entities within containers DELETE: Delete entities CHANGE_PERMISSIONS: Modify ACL permissions CHANGE_SETTINGS: Modify entity settings MODERATE: Moderate forum discussions (projects) synapse items like Submission Evaluation support different permission types covered document.

title: Access Control

title: Access Control
text: Internal Teams: Grant READ/DOWNLOAD collaborators Data Owners: Maintain full permissions (including UPDATE/DELETE) Public Data: Use public principal (273949) open datasets

title: Access Control

code: batch_1_folder <- batch_1_folder |> synSyncFromSynapse(download_file = FALSE)  # Loop over all of the files and set their annotations for (file_batch_1 in batch_1_folder$files) {   # Grab and print the existing annotations this File may already have   existing_annotations_for_file <- file_batch_1$annotations    cat(     "Got the annotations for File:", paste0(file_batch_1$name, ","),     "ID:", paste0(file_batch_1$id, ","),     "Annotations:", rjson::toJSON(existing_annotations_for_file), "\n"   )    # Merge the new annotations with anything existing   existing_annotations_for_file <- modifyList(     existing_annotations_for_file, annotation_values   )    file_batch_1 <- file_batch_1 |>     synSetProperties(annotations = existing_annotations_for_file) |>     synStore()   cat(     "Set the annotations for File:", paste0(file_batch_1$name, ","),     "ID:", paste0(file_batch_1$id, ","),     "Annotations:", rjson::toJSON(existing_annotations_for_file), "\n"   ) } Batch 1 Folder ID: syn53205629 Got the annotations for File: SRR12345678_R1.fastq.gz, ID: syn53205687, Annotations: {} Set the annotations for File: SRR12345678_R1.fastq.gz, ID: syn53205687, Annotations: {'assay': ['SCRNA-seq'], 'species': ['Homo sapiens'], 'dataType': ['geneExpression'], 'fileFormat': ['fastq']} Got the annotations for File: SRR12345678_R2.fastq.gz, ID: syn53205688, Annotations: {} Set the annotations for File: SRR12345678_R2.fastq.gz, ID: syn53205688, Annotations: {'assay': ['SCRNA-seq'], 'species': ['Homo sapiens'], 'dataType': ['geneExpression'], 'fileFormat': ['fastq']}

code: # First, get the submission status status <- SubmissionStatus(id = SUBMISSION_ID) |> synGet() print(sprintf("Retrieved submission status for submission %s", SUBMISSION_ID)) print(sprintf("Current status: %s", status$status))  # Update the submission status with scoring information status$status <- "SCORED" status$submission_annotations <- list(   accuracy = list(0.85),   precision = list(0.82),   feedback = list("Good performance!"),   validation_errors = "None detected",   score_errors = "None detected" )  # Store the updated status updated_status <- status |> synStore() print("Successfully scored submission!") print(sprintf("Status: %s", updated_status$status)) print("Annotations added:") for (key in names(updated_status$submission_annotations)) {   print(sprintf("  %s: %s", key, paste(unlist(updated_status$submission_annotations[[key]]), collapse = ", "))) }

code: # First, get all submission statuses that need updating statuses_to_update <- synGetAllSubmissionStatuses(   evaluation_id = EVALUATION_ID,   status = "RECEIVED" # Get submissions that haven't been scored yet )  print(sprintf("Found %d submissions to batch update", length(statuses_to_update)))  if (length(statuses_to_update) > 0) {   # Update each status with validation information   for (i in seq_along(statuses_to_update)) {     status <- statuses_to_update[[i]]     status$status <- "VALIDATED"     status$submission_annotations <- list(       validation_status = list("PASSED"),       validation_timestamp = list("2024-11-24T10:30:00Z"),       batch_number = list(i),       validator = list("automated_system")     )   }    # Perform batch update   batch_response <- synBatchUpdateSubmissionStatuses(     evaluation_id = EVALUATION_ID,     statuses = statuses_to_update,     is_first_batch = TRUE,     is_last_batch = TRUE   )    print("Batch update completed successfully!")   print(batch_response) } else {   print("No submissions found with 'RECEIVED' status to update") }

title: Submissions, SubmissionStatuses, SubmissionBundles
code: # Get all scored submission bundles for the evaluation print("Fetching all submission bundles for the evaluation...")  bundles <- as.list(SubmissionBundle() |> synGetEvaluationSubmissionBundles(   evaluation_id = EVALUATION_ID,   status = "SCORED" # Only get scored submissions ))  print(sprintf("Found %d scored submission bundles", length(bundles)))  first_bundles <- head(bundles, 5) # Show first 5 for (i in seq_along(first_bundles)) {   submission <- first_bundles[[i]]$submission   status <- first_bundles[[i]]$submission_status    print(sprintf("Bundle %d:", i))   if (!is.null(submission)) {     print(sprintf("  Submission ID: %s", submission$id))     print(sprintf("  Submitter: %s", submission$submitter_alias))     print(sprintf("  Entity ID: %s", submission$entity_id))     print(sprintf("  Created: %s", submission$created_on))   }    if (!is.null(status)) {     print(sprintf("  Status: %s", status$status))     print(sprintf("  Modified: %s", status$modified_on))     annotations <- status$submission_annotations     if (length(annotations) > 0) {       print("  Scores:")       for (key in names(annotations)) {         if (key %in% c("accuracy", "f1_score", "precision", "recall")) {           print(sprintf("    %s: %s", key, paste(unlist(annotations[[key]]), collapse = ", ")))         }       }     }   } }

code: # First, check if any submissions have requested cancellation all_statuses <- synGetAllSubmissionStatuses(evaluation_id = EVALUATION_ID)  cancellation_requests <- Filter(function(status) isTRUE(status$cancel_requested), all_statuses)  print(sprintf("Found %d submissions with cancellation requests", length(cancellation_requests)))  # Process cancellation requests for (status in cancellation_requests) {   print(sprintf("Processing cancellation request for submission %s", status$id))    # Update to allow cancellation (organizer decision)   status$can_cancel <- TRUE   status$status <- "CLOSED"   # submission_annotations comes back as an R copy, so update the copy   # (adding or overwriting these keys) and assign it back   annotations <- as.list(status$submission_annotations)   annotations[c("cancellation_reason", "cancelled_by", "cancellation_date")] <- list(     list("User requested cancellation"),     list("organizer"),     list("2024-11-24")   )   status$submission_annotations <- annotations    # Store the update   updated_status <- status |> synStore()   print(sprintf("  Approved cancellation for submission %s", updated_status$id)) }  # Example: Proactively allow cancellation for a specific submission print("Enabling cancellation for a specific submission...") target_status <- SubmissionStatus(id = SUBMISSION_ID) |> synGet() target_status$can_cancel <- TRUE target_status <- target_status |> synStore() print(sprintf("Cancellation enabled for submission %s", SUBMISSION_ID))

")  # Create the first table with some columns and rows table1_columns <- list(   Column(name = "sample_id", column_type = "STRING"),   Column(name = "patient_id", column_type = "STRING"),   Column(name = "age", column_type = "INTEGER"),   Column(name = "diagnosis", column_type = "STRING") )  table1 <- Table(   name = "Patient Demographics",   parent_id = project_id,   columns = table1_columns ) |> synStore() cat("Created table 1 with ID:", table1$id, "
")  # Add rows to the first table data1 <- data.frame(   sample_id = c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S6"),   patient_id = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5", "P6"),   age = c(70, 65, 72, 68, 75, 80),   diagnosis = c("Alzheimer's", "Healthy", "Alzheimer's", "Healthy", "Alzheimer's", "Healthy") ) table1 |> synUpsertRows(values = data1, primary_keys = list("sample_id"))  # Create the second table with some columns and rows table2_columns <- list(   Column(name = "sample_id", column_type = "STRING"),   Column(name = "gene", column_type = "STRING"),   Column(name = "expression_level", column_type = "DOUBLE") )  table2 <- Table(   name = "Gene Expression Data",   parent_id = project_id,   columns = table2_columns ) |> synStore() cat("Created table 2 with ID:", table2$id, "
")  # Add rows to the second table data2 <- data.frame(   sample_id = c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S7"),   gene = c("APOE", "APP", "PSEN1", "MAPT", "APP", "PSEN2"),   expression_level = c(2.5, 1.8, 3.2, 2.1, 3.5, 1.9) ) table2 |> synUpsertRows(values = data2, primary_keys = list("sample_id"))

what: 2. Create and query a basic Virtual Table
title: Virtual Tables
text: First, create simple Virtual Table selects rows table query retrieve results.
code: virtual_table <- VirtualTable(   name = "Patient Data View",   description = "A virtual table showing patient demographics",   parent_id = project_id,   defining_sql = sprintf("SELECT * FROM %s", table1$id) ) |> synStore() cat("Created Virtual Table with ID:", virtual_table$id, "\n")  query_result <- synQuery(   sprintf("SELECT * FROM %s", virtual_table$id),   include_row_id_and_row_version = FALSE ) cat("Results from the basic virtual table:\n") query_result Results from the basic virtual table:   sample_id patient_id  age    diagnosis 0        S1         P1   70  Alzheimer's 1        S2         P2   65      Healthy 2        S3         P3   72  Alzheimer's 3        S4         P4   68      Healthy 4        S5         P5   75  Alzheimer's 5        S6         P6   80      Healthy

what: 6. Create a Virtual Table with aggregation
title: Virtual Tables
text: Finally, can create Virtual Table aggregates data using functions like COUNT, along GROUP .
code: virtual_table <- VirtualTable(   name = "Diagnosis Count",   description = "A virtual table showing the count of patients by diagnosis",   parent_id = project_id,   defining_sql = sprintf("SELECT diagnosis, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM %s GROUP BY diagnosis", table1$id) ) |> synStore() cat("Created Virtual Table with ID:", virtual_table$id, "\n")  query_result <- synQuery(   sprintf("SELECT * FROM %s", virtual_table$id),   include_row_id_and_row_version = FALSE ) cat("Results from the virtual table with aggregation:\n") query_result Results from the virtual table with aggregation:      diagnosis  patient_count 0  Alzheimer's              3 1      Healthy              3

text: Wikis Synapse provide rich documentation collaborative content projects, folders, files, datasets, entities. support markdown formatting, file attachments, hierarchical organization, version history, custom ordering. code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 1: Chat with the baseline Synapse Agent     # You can chat with the same agent which is available in the Synapse UI     # at https://www.synapse.org/Chat:default. By default, this "baseline" agent     # is used when a registration ID is not provided. In the background,     # the Agent class will start a session and set that new session as the     # current session if one is not already set.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_agent = Agent()     my_agent |> synPrompt(         prompt = "Can you tell me about the AD Knowledge Portal dataset?",         enable_trace = TRUE,         print_response = TRUE     )  ## Example 2: Register and chat with a custom agent     # Only available for internal users (Sage Bionetworks employees).     #     # Alternatively, you can register a custom agent and chat with it provided     # you have already created it.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_agent = Agent(cloud_agent_id = "foo") |> synRegister()     my_agent |> synPrompt(         prompt = "Hello",         enable_trace = TRUE,         print_response = TRUE     )  ## Example 3: Prompt an existing custom agent     # If you have already registered a custom agent, you can chat with it by     # constructing an Agent with its registration ID and sending it a prompt.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_agent = Agent(registration_id = "foo")     my_agent |> synPrompt(         prompt = "Hello",         enable_trace = TRUE,         print_response = TRUE     )  ## Advanced Example: Start and prompt multiple sessions     # Here, we connect to a custom agent and start one session with the prompt "Hello".     # In the background, this first session is being set as the current session     # and future prompts will be sent to this session by default. If we want to send a     # prompt to a different session, we can do so by starting it and calling synPrompt again,     # but with our new session as an argument. We now have two sessions, both stored in the     # my_agent$sessions named list. After the second prompt, my_second_session is now     # the current session.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_agent = Agent(registration_id = "foo")      my_agent |> synPrompt(         prompt = "Hello",         enable_trace = TRUE,         print_response = TRUE     )      my_second_session = my_agent |> synStartSession()     my_agent |> synPrompt(         prompt = "Hello again",         enable_trace = TRUE,         print_response = TRUE,         session = my_second_session     ) } # }

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 1: Create a new dataset from a list of EntityRefs.     # Dataset items consist of references to Synapse Files using an Entity Reference.     # If you are adding items to a Dataset directly, you must provide them in the form of     # an EntityRef class instance.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_entity_refs = list(EntityRef(id = "syn1234"), EntityRef(id = "syn1235"), EntityRef(id = "syn1236"))     my_dataset = Dataset(parent_id = "syn987", name = "my-new-dataset", items = my_entity_refs)     my_dataset |> synStore()  ## Example 2: Add entities to an existing dataset.     # Using synAddItem(), you can add Synapse entities that are Files, Folders, or EntityRefs that point to a Synapse entity.     # If the entity is a Folder (or an EntityRef that points to a folder), all of the child Files     # within the Folder will be added to the Dataset recursively.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_dataset = Dataset(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()      # Add a file to the dataset     my_dataset |> synAddItem(File(id = "syn1235"))      # Add a folder to the dataset     # All child files are recursively added to the dataset     my_dataset |> synAddItem(Folder(id = "syn1236"))      # Add an entity reference to the dataset     my_dataset |> synAddItem(EntityRef(id = "syn1237", version = 1L))      my_dataset |> synStore()  ## Example 3: Remove entities from a dataset.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_dataset = Dataset(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()      # Remove a file from the dataset     my_dataset |> synRemoveItem(File(id = "syn1235"))      # Remove a folder from the dataset     # All child files are recursively removed from the dataset     my_dataset |> synRemoveItem(Folder(id = "syn1236"))      # Remove an entity reference from the dataset     my_dataset |> synRemoveItem(EntityRef(id = "syn1237", version = 1L))      my_dataset |> synStore()  ## Example 4: Query data from a dataset.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      row = synQuery(query = "SELECT * FROM syn1234 WHERE id = 'syn1235'")     print(row)  ## Example 5: Add a custom column to a dataset.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_dataset = Dataset(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()     my_dataset |> synAddColumn(Column(name = "my_annotation", column_type = "STRING"))     my_dataset |> synStore()  ## Example 6: Update custom column values in a dataset.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_dataset = Dataset(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()     # my_annotation must already exist in the dataset as a custom column     modified_data = data.frame(         id = c("syn1234"),         my_annotation = c("good data")     )     my_dataset |> synUpdateRows(values = modified_data, primary_keys = list("id"), dry_run = FALSE)  ## Example 7: Save a snapshot of a dataset.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_dataset = Dataset(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()     my_dataset |> synSnapshot(comment = "My first snapshot", label = "My first snapshot")  ## Example 8: Deleting a dataset.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      Dataset(id = "syn4567") |> synDelete() } # }

Example 5: Retrieve and update annotations for a materialized view.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      materialized_view = MaterializedView(id = "syn12345") |> synGet()     materialized_view = materialized_view |>         synSetProperties(             annotations = append(                 materialized_view$annotations,                 list(key1 = "value1", key2 = "value2")             )         ) |>         synStore()     print("Updated annotations for Materialized View.")  ## Example 6: Create a materialized view with a JOIN clause.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      defining_sql = "     SELECT t1.column1 AS new_column1, t2.column2 AS new_column2     FROM syn12345 t1     JOIN syn67890 t2     ON t1.id = t2.foreign_id     "      materialized_view = MaterializedView(         name = "Join Materialized View",         description = "A materialized view with a JOIN clause",         parent_id = "syn11111",         defining_sql = defining_sql     ) |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Created Materialized View with ID: %s", materialized_view$id))  ## Example 7: Create a materialized view with a LEFT JOIN clause.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      defining_sql = "     SELECT t1.column1 AS new_column1, t2.column2 AS new_column2     FROM syn12345 t1     LEFT JOIN syn67890 t2     ON t1.id = t2.foreign_id     "      materialized_view = MaterializedView(         name = "Left Join Materialized View",         description = "A materialized view with a LEFT JOIN clause",         parent_id = "syn11111",         defining_sql = defining_sql     ) |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Created Materialized View with ID: %s", materialized_view$id))  ## Example 8: Create a materialized view with a RIGHT JOIN clause.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      defining_sql = "     SELECT t1.column1 AS new_column1, t2.column2 AS new_column2     FROM syn12345 t1     RIGHT JOIN syn67890 t2     ON t1.id = t2.foreign_id     "      materialized_view = MaterializedView(         name = "Right Join Materialized View",         description = "A materialized view with a RIGHT JOIN clause",         parent_id = "syn11111",         defining_sql = defining_sql     ) |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Created Materialized View with ID: %s", materialized_view$id))  ## Example 9: Create a materialized view with a UNION clause.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      defining_sql = "     SELECT column1 AS new_column1, column2 AS new_column2     FROM syn12345     UNION     SELECT column1 AS new_column1, column2 AS new_column2     FROM syn67890     "      materialized_view = MaterializedView(         name = "Union Materialized View",         description = "A materialized view with a UNION clause",         parent_id = "syn11111",         defining_sql = defining_sql     ) |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Created Materialized View with ID: %s", materialized_view$id)) } # }

")     bound_schema      # Create a file within the project with invalid annotations to generate invalid results     invalid_file1 = File(         path = FILE_PATH,  # assumes you have something here or adjust path         parent_id = PROJECT_ID     )     invalid_file1$annotations = list(foo = 123, bar = "not_an_integer")  # both invalid     invalid_file1 = invalid_file1 |> synStore()     cat("Created file with invalid annotations
")     Sys.sleep(2)  # Allow time for processing      # Get invalid validation results     # synGetInvalidValidation() returns a Python generator, wrapped as a     # GeneratorWrapper -- materialize it with as.list() before iterating,     # since R's for() can't drive a Python generator directly.     invalid_results = as.list(test_project |> synGetInvalidValidation())     cat("Invalid validation items found:
")     for (child in invalid_results) {         cat(sprintf("Invalid validation item: %s
", child))     } } # }

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 1: Create a table with data without specifying columns     # This API is setup to allow the data to define which columns are created on the     # Synapse table automatically. The limitation with this behavior is that the     # columns created will only be of the following types:      # - STRING     # - LARGETEXT     # - INTEGER     # - DOUBLE     # - BOOLEAN     # - DATE      # The determination of the column type is based on the data that is passed in     # using the pandas function     # infer_dtype (https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.api.types.infer_dtype.html).     # If you need a more specific column type, or need to add options to the columns     # follow the examples below.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      my_data = data.frame(         my_string_column = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),         my_integer_column = c(1, 2, 3, 4),         my_double_column = c(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0),         my_boolean_column = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)     )      table = Table(         name = "my_table",         parent_id = "syn1234"     ) |> synStore()      table |> synStoreRows(values = my_data, schema_storage_strategy = "INFER_FROM_DATA")      # Prints out the stored data about this specific column     table$columns[["my_string_column"]]  ## Example 2: Rename an existing column     # This examples shows how you may retrieve a table from synapse, rename a column,     # and then store the table back in synapse.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      table = Table(         name = "my_table",         parent_id = "syn1234"     ) |> synGet()      # You may also get the table by id:     table = Table(id = "syn4567") |> synGet()      table$columns[["my_old_column"]]$name = "my_new_column"      # Before the data is stored in synapse you'll still be able to use the old key to access the column entry     table$columns[["my_old_column"]]      table = table |> synStore()      # After the data is stored in synapse you'll be able to use the new key to access the column entry     table$columns[["my_new_column"]]  ## Example 3: Create a table with a list of columns     # A list of columns may be passed in when creating a new table. The order of the     # columns in the list will be the order they are stored in Synapse. If the table     # already exists and you create the Table instance in this way the columns will     # be appended to the end of the existing columns.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      columns = list(         Column(name = "my_string_column", column_type = "STRING"),         Column(name = "my_integer_column", column_type = "INTEGER"),         Column(name = "my_double_column", column_type = "DOUBLE"),         Column(name = "my_boolean_column", column_type = "BOOLEAN")     )      table = Table(         name = "my_table",         parent_id = "syn1234",         columns = columns     )      table |> synStore()  ## Example 4: Creating a table with a named list of columns     # When specifying a number of columns via a named list setting the name attribute     # on the Column object is optional. When it is not specified it will be     # pulled from the key of the named list.     library(synapser)     synLogin()      columns = list(         my_string_column = Column(column_type = "STRING"),         my_integer_column = Column(column_type = "INTEGER"),         my_double_column = Column(column_type = "DOUBLE"),         my_boolean_column = Column(column_type = "BOOLEAN")     )      table = Table(         name = "my_table",         parent_id = "syn1234",         columns = columns     )      table |> synStore() } # }

Example 8: Comprehensive File options     # Download file with custom location and collision handling:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      file_entity = synGet(         synapse_id = "syn123456",         file_options = FileOptions(             download_file = TRUE,             download_location = "/path/to/download/",             if_collision = "overwrite.local"         )     )     print(sprintf("Downloaded file: %s to %s", file_entity$name, file_entity$path))  ## Example 10: Combining multiple options     # Get a File with both activity and custom download options:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      file_entity = synGet(         synapse_id = "syn123456",         activity_options = ActivityOptions(include_activity = TRUE),         file_options = FileOptions(             download_file = FALSE         )     )     print(sprintf("File: %s (activity included: %s)", file_entity$name, !is.null(file_entity$activity)))  ## title: synStore — synStore
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 1: Storing a file     # Store a file to Synapse:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      file = File(path = "/path/to/file.txt", parent_id = "syn123456")     stored_file = file |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Stored file: %s (ID: %s)", stored_file$name, stored_file$id))  ## Example 2: Storing a file with custom options     # Store a file with custom options:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      file = File(path = "/path/to/file.txt", parent_id = "syn123456")     stored_file = file |> synStore(         file_options = StoreFileOptions(             synapse_store = TRUE,             content_type = "text/plain",             merge_existing_annotations = TRUE         )     )     print(sprintf("Stored file: %s", stored_file$name))  ## Example 3: Storing a folder     # Store a folder to Synapse:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      folder = Folder(name = "My Folder", parent_id = "syn123456")     stored_folder = folder |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Stored folder: %s (ID: %s)", stored_folder$name, stored_folder$id))  ## Example 4: Storing a project     # Store a project to Synapse:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      project = Project(name = "My Project")     stored_project = project |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Stored project: %s (ID: %s)", stored_project$name, stored_project$id))  ## Example 5: Storing a table     # Store a table to Synapse:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      table = Table(         name = "My Table",         parent_id = "syn123456",         columns = list(Column(name = "col1", column_type = "STRING", maximum_size = 50L))     )     stored_table = table |> synStore(         table_options = StoreTableOptions(dry_run = FALSE, job_timeout = 600L)     )     print(sprintf("Stored table: %s (ID: %s)", stored_table$name, stored_table$id))  ## Example 6: Storing a link     # Store a link to Synapse:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      link = Link(name = "My Link", parent_id = "syn123456", target_id = "syn789")     stored_link = link |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Stored link: %s (ID: %s)", stored_link$name, stored_link$id))  ## Example 7: Storing with parent parameter     # Store an entity by passing the parent as a parameter:     library(synapser)     synLogin()      parent_folder = Folder(id = "syn123456")     file = File(path = "/path/to/file.txt")     stored_file = file |> synStore(parent = parent_folder)     print(sprintf("Stored file: %s in folder %s", stored_file$name, parent_folder$id))  ## Example 8: Storing an Evaluation     # Store an evaluation (challenge queue):     library(synapser)     synLogin()      evaluation = Evaluation(         name = "My Challenge Evaluation",         description = "Evaluation for my data challenge",         content_source = "syn123456"     )     stored_evaluation = evaluation |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Stored evaluation: %s (ID: %s)", stored_evaluation$name, stored_evaluation$id))  ## Example 9: Creating a Team     # Create a new team (note: Teams use create, not update):     library(synapser)     synLogin()      team = Team(         name = "My Research Team",         description = "A team for collaborative research"     )     created_team = team |> synStore()     print(sprintf("Created team: %s (ID: %s)", created_team$name, created_team$id)) } # }
